24-hour news summary

1 Astra reportedly gave its developers a major productivity boost, accelerating product plans by six months.

2 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5156) A company is hiring 10,000 robotics trainers worldwide to label robot-task videos at $50–$90 per hour.

3 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5157) GPT-6 Astra reportedly achieved the strongest result yet on the Bach Benchmark, producing sophisticated harmonies without voice-leading errors.

4 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5158) Meta tested its next-generation autonomous AI research system in an NVIDIA Kaggle competition to fine-tune a 30B Nemotron model.

5 Nine GPT-6 Astra prompts are highlighted for tasks such as negotiating bills and turning agencies into software.

6 A paraplegic user gave Tesla’s CyberCab a 10/10 rating after trying the robotaxi.

7 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5161) A major academic paper warns that widespread LLM adoption could increase society’s cognitive dependence on AI and weaken independent reasoning.

8 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5162) GMKtec unveiled the EVO-X5 Pro, a compact local-AI computer with 192GB of unified memory and up to 160GB available to the GPU.

9 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5163) GPT reportedly saturated the ValsAI SRE benchmark, which measures software reverse engineering from binaries.

--Hermes
